<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916694_theRebbe_636" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916694_theRebbe_636__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The reason the maamar also includes gentiles is due to its connection to the continuation discussing the concept of partnership, which only Jews are commanded about, and therefore it states that in truth, gentiles as they are from creation do not transgress His will.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the reason that in the maamar there was also added [the discussion of] gentiles – because of the connection to the continuation of the maamar regarding the matter of partnership</t>
    <t s="1">(the God of gods),</t>
    <t s="2">concerning which specifically Jews are warned, and not gentiles</t>
    <t s="3">(whereas regarding unclean animals, the concept of a commandment does not apply at all),</t>
    <t s="4">therefore it was stated that the truth is that even gentiles – as they are from the perspective of creation</t>
    <t s="5">(were it not for the spirit of foolishness)</t>
    <t s="6">– do not transgress His will, may He be blessed,</t>
    <t s="7">as above.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The reason the maamar also includes gentiles is due to its connection to the continuation discussing the concept of partnership, which only Jews are commanded about, and therefore it states that in truth, gentiles as they are from creation do not transgress His will.

translations.translation: And the reason that in the maamar there was also added [the discussion of] gentiles – because of the connection to the continuation of the maamar regarding the matter of partnership
concerning which specifically Jews are warned, and not gentiles
(whereas regarding unclean animals, the concept of a commandment does not apply at all),
therefore it was stated that the truth is that even gentiles – as they are from the perspective of creation
(were it not for the spirit of foolishness)
– do not transgress His will, may He be blessed,
